activity.notes: Pompey was a leading general and statesman of the late Roman Republic. ATLAS uses 70–48 BCE as a representative public-leadership Activity beginning with his first consulship and ending with his death after Pharsalus. This does not claim one continuous office: within the interval he held consulships in 70, 55 and 52 BCE, extraordinary military commands, and major political authority. The general_activity basis is used specifically to avoid flattening those distinct constitutional offices into a fictitious continuous consulship.

sources.title: Pompey the Great — British Museum
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Pompey as a Roman statesman and general of the late Republic, 106–48 BCE, and a member of the First Triumvirate.

sources.title: imperium — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary describes the extraordinary imperium granted to Pompey by the lex Gabinia in 67 BCE, illustrating his exceptional late-Republic military command.
